summary: The code path is a genuine implementation of the non-ECMA-402 localeCompare. Steps 1-4 run in spec order: RequireObjectCoercible(this), ToString(this), ToString(that), with ? propagation. Both strings are NFC-normalized and compared by code units, returning -1/0/1. That gives a total preorder and +0 for canonically equivalent strings, as the spec requires. The spec allows an implementation-defined comparator when no host locale is used, so this is not a made-up result. The one defect is in the comments: the NOTE's canonical-equivalence examples were rewritten from the spec's \u escape sequences into literal characters. Each example now compares a string with an identical-looking copy of itself, so the spec quotation is corrupted. That is an unrequested change to spec text.
